nicknames: The Dirt Track of the Pilbara

main_dirt.bias_notes: Anti-clockwise (left-handed). Port Hedland is a premier WA Pilbara dirt oval featuring a specialized red sand/oil-dirt surface and a short 300m home straight. The track creates severe kickback, heavily favoring early speed ('E') and front-runners that command the rail. Deep closers ('C') suffer a massive disadvantage eating kickback down the short 300m stretch.
main_dirt.post_bias: In 1200m and 1300m sprint events, inside barriers (1–4) hold an immense advantage by allowing runners to grab the lead or rail, completely avoiding dirt kickback. In 1400m, 1600m, and 2200m Port Hedland Cup routes, horses that clear the field early to secure the fence dominate.

handicapping_angles.pilbara_dirt_surface_specialists: Port Hedland's red dirt track is highly specialized. Heavily upgrade horses with proven track-and-distance form on WA dirt tracks (Broome, Roebourne, Carnarvon, Newman). Be cautious with Perth turf shippers (Ascot/Belmont) making their first start on dirt unless possessing elite 1st-call gate speed.
handicapping_angles.extreme_front_running_kickback_bias: Over 75% of winners at Port Hedland race on or near the lead. Kickback is thick and abrasive; horses forced to race back in the pack often yield. Aggressively upgrade lone early speed ('E') and tactical pressers ('P') drawn inside.
handicapping_angles.port_hedland_cup_carnival_stamina: During the Port Hedland Cup (2200m) winter carnival in July/August, staying toughness on dirt is paramount. Look for proven staying lines with strong 2nd-call positioning.
handicapping_angles.wa_country_weight_penalty: In WA Country Benchmark handicaps, top weights carrying 60kg+ face a strict burden on heavy dirt. Value fit, well-weighted drop-downs or skilled claiming apprentices taking weight off top-rated contenders.
